verses.zh: （大卫的赞美诗。）我的　神我的王啊，我要尊崇你！我要永永远远称颂你的名！
verses.en: A psalm of praise; by David.I will extol you, my God, O King.I will praise your name continually.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 145. The psalmist praises God because he is a just and merciful king who cares for his people.
verses.commentary:
145:1 "I will extol You" Notice the
personal element expressed so often in Ps. 145:1-7. This is clearly seen by the
phrase, "my God." It is obvious that personal faith is the beginning point in
understanding the God

- in creation

- in history

This opening strophe (i.e., Ps. 145:1-7) has several
COHORTATIVES or IMPERFECTS used in a COHORTATIVE sense.

- I will extol You, Ps. 145:1 ‒ BDB 926, KB 1202, Polel
IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense

- I will bless Your name, Ps. 145:1 ‒ BDB 138, KB 159, Piel COHORTATIVES

- I will bless You, Ps. 145:2 ‒ BDB 138, KB 159, Piel IMPERFECT
used in a COHORTATIVE sense

- I will praise Your name, Ps. 145:2 ‒ BDB 237, KB 248, Piel COHORTATIVE

- I will meditate on Your wonderful works, Ps. 145:5 ‒ BDB 967, KB 1319, Qal
COHORTATIVE

- I will tell of Your greatness, Ps. 145:6 ‒ BDB 707, KB 765, Piel IMPERFECT
used in a COHORTATIVE sense

True faithful followers must express their faith and praise of YHWH.

▣"my God" This is the Hebrew title Eloah, which is the SINGULAR form
of Elohim.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

▣ "O King" YHWH was the true King of
Israel (cf. 1 Sam. 8:7). The earthly king was only a mere representative of the
heavenly King (cf. Ps. 10:16; 29:10; 98:6).

▣ "I will bless Your name" The concept of "blessing" (BDB 138, VERB; 139, NOUN)
is part of the Hebrew theology related to the power of the spoken word, especially in worship. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING.

The term "name" (BDB 1027) is a Hebraic way of referring to the person. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH.

Israel's Deity is called Eloah in Ps. 145:1 but YHWH
nine times in the rest of the Psalm. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY C., D.

▣ "forever and ever" The phrase is
used in Ps. 145:1b and 2b and seems to be used in the same sense in Ps. 34:1,
which is explicitly expressed in Ps. 145:2a. It is not really an affirmation of
the afterlife but a Hebrew idiom of daily praise.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

verses.zh: 我要天天称颂你，也要永永远远赞美你的名！
verses.en: Every day I will praise you.I will praise your name continually.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or, hyperbolically, “forever.”

verses.zh: 耶和华本为大，该受大赞美；其大无法测度。
verses.en: The Lord is great and certainly worthy of praise.No one can fathom his greatness.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or, hyperbolically, “forever.”
verses.commentary:
145:3 "Great is the Lord, and highly to be praised"
This phrase became a liturgical affirmation from the thanksgiving Psalm, written for David
bringing the ark into Jerusalem (cf. 1 Chr. 16:25 [cf. Ps. 48:1; 96:4]). The psalm in 1 Chronicles 16
also has a universal emphasis. The logical implication of

- monotheism

- humans created in God's image and likeness (cf. Gen. 1:26-27) for fellowship (Gen. 3:8)

- God's promise to mankind in Gen. 3:15

demands a universal understanding of the purpose of the nation of Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "His greatness is unsearchable"
The NOUN "greatness" (BDB 153) is used of both

- God Himself ‒ 1 Chr. 29:11; Ps. 48:1; 86:10; 147:5

- His acts ‒ 2 Sam. 7:21; 1 Chr. 17:19-21

"Unsearchable" (lit. "there is no searching," i.e., NOUN CONSTRUCT)
is used in Job 5:9; 9:10; 11:7. The same concept of God's ways being far above our understanding is
expressed in Ps. 139:6; Isa. 40:28; 55:8,9; Rom. 11:33.

verses.zh: 这代要对那代颂赞你的作为，也要传扬你的大能。
verses.en: One generation will praise your deeds to anotherand tell about your mighty acts.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and concerning his greatness there is no searching.”
verses.commentary:
145:4 "One generation shall praise Your works to another" This is an emphasis on Israel passing
on their faith to their children (cf. Deut. 4:9,10; 6:7,20-25; 11:19; 32:7,46; Ps. 22:30,31).

The VERBS of Ps. 145:4 are
IMPERFECTS but they may be JUSSIVE in meaning,
describing the psalmist's wishes/prayers. The same is
true of Ps. 145:6 and 7 (NET Bible, p. 1009).

▣ "Your mighty acts" This emphasis is
on the God who acts in fidelity to His covenant promises, cf. Ps.
145:4,5,6,7,12. Usually this term refers to God's past redemptive acts, such as
the Exodus.

verses.zh: 我要默念你威严的尊荣和你奇妙的作为。
verses.en: I will focus on your honor and majestic splendorand your amazing deeds.[NOTE:1]
notes: The prefixed verbal forms in v. 4 are understood as imperfects, indicating how the psalmist expects his audience to respond to his praise. Another option is to take the forms as jussives, indicating the psalmist’s wish, “may one generation praise…and tell about.”
verses.commentary:
145:5 "On the glorious splendor of Your majesty" Human vocabulary is quite inadequate to
express the glory of God (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY [OT]). Here is a series of words which are linked together in order to
catch the glorious nature of God (i.e., vv. 5-7).

- glorious splendor ‒ BDB 214, cf. 1 Chr. 16:27; Ps. 29:4; 90:16; 96:6; 104:1; 111:3; Isa. 2:10,19,21

- majesty ‒ BDB 217, cf. 1 Chr. 16:27; 29:11; Ps. 96:6; 111:3; 148:13

- wondrous works ‒ BDB 810, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: WONDERFUL THINGS

- awesome acts, v. 6

- greatmess, v. 6

- abundant goodness, v. 7

▣ "I will meditate" Faithful followers
will remember YHWH's great acts, cf. Ps. 145:7 (cf. Ps. 119:27). It is amazing how many times in
the Bible faithful followers are admonished to remember what God has done! They can trust God amidst the uncertainties of
present reality because of His faithfulness in human's past reality.

verses.zh: 人要传说你可畏之事的能力；我也要传扬你的大德。
verses.en: They will proclaim[NOTE:1] the power of your awesome acts.I will declare your great deeds.
notes: Heb “the splendor of the glory of your majesty, and the matters of your amazing deeds I will ponder.”
verses.commentary:
145:6 "Men shall speak of the power of Your
awesome acts" This is the first allusion to "all men," which is the
common refrain of Ps. 145:8-21. This has contextual potential of including all
Gentiles, as well as Israelites. However, it may be a literary necessity which is
produced by the acrostic form of writing.

Notice the number of ways the psalmist refers to YHWH's works.

- Your works, Ps. 145:4a, 9b, 10a

- Your mighty acts, Ps. 145:4b, 12

- Your wonderful works, Ps. 145:5b

- Your awesome acts, Ps. 145:6a

This refers to

- the creation and/or the flood

- acts of forgiveness and restoration

- call of Abraham and the Patriarchs

- the Exodus

- the Conquest

- victories in battle

- etc.

Heb “the fame of the greatness of your goodness.”

145:7 "eagerly utter" The VERB (BDB 615, KB 665, Hiphil
IMPERFECT) means "to bubble up." It is used

▣ "Your righteousness" The term
"righteousness" (BDB 842) comes from the Hebrew root, "a measuring reed." It can
be used in two ways in the OT:

- God's transcendent holiness and eternality

- His acts of redeeming Israel

This is where most modern
translations insert the missing nun phrase (i.e., finish the acrostic) from the LXX, Peshitta and
Vulgate, and one Hebrew manuscript of the Dead Sea Scrolls (i.e., 11QPsa),
"God is faithful in all His words and gracious in all His deeds." This is very
similar to Ps. 145:17. The UBS Text Project, p. 439, gives the inclusion a "B" rating.

verses.zh: 凡跌倒的，耶和华将他们扶持；凡被压下的，将他们扶起。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The Lord supports all who falland lifts up all who are bent over.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “a kingdom of all ages.”

Psalm 145 is an acrostic psalm, with each successive verse beginning with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet. However, in the traditional Hebrew (Masoretic) text of Psalm 145 there is no verse beginning with the letter nun. One would expect such a verse to appear as the fourteenth verse, between the (מ) (mem) and (ס) (samek) verses. Several ancient witnesses, including one medieval Hebrew manuscript, the Qumran scroll from cave 11, the LXX, and the Syriac, supply the missing (נ) (nun) verse, which reads as follows: “The Lord is reliable in all his words, and faithful in all his deeds.” One might paraphrase this as follows: “The Lord’s words are always reliable; his actions are always faithful.” Scholars are divided as to the originality of this verse. L. C. Allen argues for its inclusion on the basis of structural considerations (Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 294-95), but there is no apparent explanation for why, if original, it would have been accidentally omitted. The psalm may be a partial acrostic, as in Pss 25 and 34 (see M. Dahood, Psalms [AB], 3:335). The glaring omission of the nun line would have invited a later redactor to add such a line.
verses.commentary:
145:14 "The Lord sustains all who fall"
Psalm 145:14-16 speaks of God
providing faithful followers' physical needs, while Ps. 145:17-21 speaks of God
providing for their spiritual needs.

Notice the repetitive use of the inclusive term "all"
(כל, KB 474, vv. 14a, 14b, 15a, 17a, 18a, 18b, 20a, 21b).

verses.zh: 万民都举目仰望你；你随时给他们食物。
verses.en: Everything looks to you in anticipation,[NOTE:1] and you provide them with food on a regular basis.[NOTE:2]
notes: Perhaps “discouraged” (see Ps 57:6).
Heb “the eyes of all wait for you.”
verses.commentary:
145:15 "The eyes of all look to You"
These verses state that God provides food for all of His creatures, cf. Ps.
104:27,28; 136:25. This is one of the tasks of Elohim. God as creator, provider, and sustainer.

verses.zh: 你张手，使有生气的都随愿饱足。

notes: Heb “and you give to them their food in its season” (see Ps 104:27).
verses.commentary:
145:16 This is the concept of
"Providence." God creates and sustains this planet and all its life forms. This
action in the OT is attributed to Elohim.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide
commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of
the Bible. Each of us must walk n the light we have. You, the Bible, and the

These discussion questions are provided to help you think
through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be
thought provoking, not definitive.

- List the praise-worthy attributes of God.

- This Psalm refers to YHWH's acts in several verses and in several ways. What acts is it referring to?

- How does Ps. 145:8-16 (and 145:21) communicate YHWH's universal love?

- Who are "the godly ones" of Ps. 145:10?

- Who are "the sons of men" of Ps. 145:12?

- Does the OT focus on an eternal kingdom or a millennium?

- How does the "transcendence" of Ps. 145:5 relate to the "eminence" of Ps. 145:18?

- List the four conditions of Ps. 145:18-20 which relate to faithful followers.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original
author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one
and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This is an acrostic Psalm. There are other examples in the Psalter.

- Psalm 9 and 10

- Psalm 25

- Psalm 34

- Psalm 37

- Psalm 111

- Psalm 112

- Psalm 119

- Psalm 145

Acrostics can also be seen in Prov. 31:16-31 and Lamentations 1; 2; 3; and 4.
There are 22 letters in the Hebrew alphabet. There are only 21 verses in this
Psalm, so obviously one letter is omitted. The Hebrew "N" has somehow been
misplaced in the Masoretic text (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM). It is included in all of the ancient
versions—the Septuagint, the Vulgate, and the Peshitta. We find it in one
Hebrew manuscript in the Dead Sea Scrolls, 11QPsa.

- This Psalm is about the character of Israel's God and His acts which reveal that character.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT).

- This Psalm has a unique universal element which can be seen in Ps. 145:8-21. This is one
of the unique glimpses into the heart of God which shows His love for all peoples of the earth
and of His desire for all people to know Him by faith (cf. Ezek. 18:23,32; John 3:16; 4:42;
1 Tim. 2:4; 4:10; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:1; 4:14)
